In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and synthesis of new fluorescent probes that can be turned on by a metal ion and off by a second metal ion.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the fluorescence of L2 is turned on by Zn2+ and H+ binding, and turned off by the addition of a second Zn2+.

the Zn2+ ion, in the presence of a suitable proton donor, is able to switch on the fluorescence emission of a 9 methyl phen moiety, while the presence of a Cu2+ ion quenches the fluorescence emission of the same chromophore.
the Zn2+ ion can be regarded as a switch on for the fluorescence of phen ligands, provided the ligand is protonated.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the fluorescence emission of polypyridine ligands can be switched on by simultaneous protonation and metal binding, provided that the ligand contains an amine chain that is able to bind the proton and metal ions simultaneously.
the fluorescence emission of the L2 phen moiety is switched on and off by the binding of Zn2+ ions and protons, respectively.
the simultaneous protonation and Zn2+ binding of L2 switches on the emission of the 9 methyl phen moiety, whereas the same process with L1 switches on the emission from the bpy unit.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the fluorescence emission of polypyridine ligands can be switched on and off by binding Zn2+ and H+ ions simultaneously, a process that is not possible for Cu2+.
the fluorescence emission of a ligand with a PET quenching mechanism can be turned on by the binding of two different metal ions, one of which is a H+ ion, which acts as a PET blocker.
, in contrast to the common belief, the Zn2+ ion is not necessarily a quenching metal, and can be successfully used to enhance the fluorescence emission of polypyridine ligands.
